title: Vomiting student
presenting_complaint: Two days of vomiting and abdominal pain, with increasing thirst and polyuria.
history: 19 y.o. male university student, type 1 diabetes since age 11 on basal-bolus insulin. Two days of vomiting and abdominal pain; he stopped his insulin because he "wasn't eating". Increasing thirst and polyuria. No diarrhoea. Denies alcohol or drug use. No known drug allergies.

findings.name: Hydration status
findings.value: dry mucous membranes, capillary refill 4 s

findings.name: Venous blood gas
findings.value: pH 7.08, bicarbonate 7 mmol/L, glucose 28.4 mmol/L, potassium 5.6 mmol/L, lactate 2.1 mmol/L

diagnosis_options.label: Diabetic ketoacidosis
diagnosis_options.explanation: Correct diagnosis: hyperglycaemia, ketonaemia and metabolic acidosis (pH 7.08, bicarbonate 7 mmol/L) in a patient with type 1 diabetes who stopped insulin.

diagnosis_options.label: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state
diagnosis_options.explanation: Hyperglycaemia is right, but this is ketoacidosis (marked ketonaemia and severe metabolic acidosis).

diagnosis_options.label: Acute pancreatitis
diagnosis_options.explanation: Abdominal pain and vomiting can occur, but lipase is normal and the metabolic picture is that of ketoacidosis.

diagnosis_options.label: Gastroenteritis
diagnosis_options.explanation: Vomiting and abdominal pain may suggest it, but there is no diarrhoea and the acidosis, ketonaemia and hyperglycaemia indicate ketoacidosis.

diagnosis_options.label: Sepsis from urinary tract infection
diagnosis_options.explanation: Urinalysis shows no nitrites or leukocytes, and the presentation is explained by diabetic ketoacidosis.

management_options.label: IV 0.9% saline resuscitation
management_options.explanation: Essential initial treatment for the marked dehydration and shock.

management_options.label: Continue long-acting basal insulin
management_options.explanation: Reasonable and helpful to prevent rebound ketogenesis, but not the primary acute treatment.

management_options.label: Potassium replacement guided by hourly levels once K+ falls below 5.5
management_options.explanation: Essential: insulin will drive potassium intracellularly, so potassium must be replaced as levels fall.

management_options.label: IV sodium bicarbonate
management_options.explanation: Not recommended at this pH and potentially harmful.

management_options.label: Insulin bolus plus variable-rate sliding scale instead of a fixed-rate infusion
management_options.explanation: Harmful; a fixed-rate IV insulin infusion is the recommended approach.
